findings.finding: triage-cli-runner.ts did not thread deps.homeDir into its resolveUv() calls, unlike the sibling fix in grade-runner.ts which passes homeDir through — an asymmetry between the two runners fixed in the same commit. Currently harmless (no production caller overrides homeDir today) but left the PATH-augmentation env always resolving against the real os.homedir() regardless of an injected homeDir. Fixed in follow-up: both triageWriteAvailability() and runTriageCli() now pass homeDir: deps.homeDir to resolveUv().
findings.suggestion: Thread homeDir through for symmetry with grade-runner.ts — done.

findings.finding: routes/grade.ts's header comment still said 'fixed python binary', stale after the spawn moved to `uv run --project <plugin-root>`. Fixed in follow-up: comment updated to describe the uv run --project spawn.
findings.suggestion: Update the stale doc comment — done.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: triage-cli-runner's `uv run --python ">=3.11"` (no --project) runs triage_cli.py in an isolated/ad-hoc environment with no silent-fallback risk. — Without --project/--no-project, uv run walks up from the SPAWNING PROCESS's cwd (never the script's own path) looking for an ambient pyproject.toml to activate. Neither runner sets `cwd` on execFile, so discovery ran from wherever the Node server process started, not from shared/scripts/tools/. Confirmed live: cwd'd into shipwright-grade's own plugin root (which HAS a pyproject.toml) and ran the triage_cli.py invocation from there — it silently succeeded against that ambient project rather than erroring, exactly the accidental-adoption risk described.

Claim under doubt: no-direct-python-spawn.test.ts's regex-based scan forecloses the regression class of a new call site spawning a raw python interpreter. — Found two additional bypasses beyond the one the external code-reviewer already caught: (a) a template-literal spawn target (execFile(`python3`, ...)) was invisible to the quote-only regex; (b) a future call site reimplementing the python3->python->py probe LOOP inline (copying the literal array from readiness-probe-run.ts, rather than calling the shared resolvePython()) would trip neither existing check, since its spawn target is a loop variable, not a direct literal or a flat single assignment.

Claim under doubt: Grade's route is read-only; this change doesn't add a write surface. — Confirmed on the real machine that uv run --project writes into the plugin's OWN cache directory (~/.claude/plugins/cache/shipwright/shipwright-grade/<version>/.venv/) on first dependency sync — something the old bare-python spawn never did. Neither the unit tests (mocked spawn) nor the E2E harness (uv-shim execs python directly, bypassing real uv sync) exercise a cold-cache first-grade or two concurrent first-syncs racing the same .venv.

Claim under doubt: resolveGradePluginRoot()'s "3 levels up" assumption could target the wrong directory. — Verified directly against the real cache: shipwright-grade/<version>/pyproject.toml and uv.lock exist exactly 3 dirname() calls up from the resolved grade.py, for the only layout actually observed in the wild. The untested defensive flat-layout fallback is internally consistent, and even a wrong target fails loudly (uv run --project <dir-without-pyproject.toml> errors clearly) rather than silently succeeding against an unintended project.

Claim under doubt: resolveUv()'s presence probe and its bin/env resolution could diverge if a caller supplies mismatched deps. — Traced both production call sites — neither ever supplies deps.homeDir/deps.baseEnv/deps.platform without also supplying a matching run, so in production both computations derive from identical process.env/os.homedir()/process.platform and are provably byte-identical today.

The regression guard can be bypassed by ordinary direct-spawn code, so it does not fully enforce the acceptance criterion that no `server/src/` call site may resolve a raw Python binary and spawn it. For example, `const py = "python3"; await spawn(py, [script], opts)` matches neither check, and a new nested file named `readiness-probe.ts` or `readiness-probe-run.ts` is blanket-allowlisted by basename. Such a regression would pass all five guard tests.
findings.suggestion: Use an AST-based scan (or a stricter source rule) that detects interpreter literals assigned to variables and subsequently passed to process-spawn APIs, and allowlist exact known file paths/expressions rather than every file sharing a basename.  The production invocation changes appear to satisfy the required `uv run --project` and `uv run --python ">=3.11"` behavior and preserve the required environment layering. However, the required regression guard is incomplete and should be strengthened before shipping. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
